changed_lines_detail: tools/round_envelope.py: net +69 lines (374 -> 443), all added, none removed except one replaced line in cmd_init; tests/test_round_envelope.py: net +150 lines (273 -> 423)
root_cause: An empty --dst reached cmd_init. _norm_path('') = os.path.abspath('') = the current working directory, so a blank destination silently resolved to the repo root. The three existing guards (guard_paths) only model containment BETWEEN the src/dst/scratch arguments; with --src pointing at a different directory all three passed, and shutil.rmtree(dst) deleted the repository root (tracked .agents/ and parts of .git/). The try/except around the removal cannot help because that rmtree SUCCEEDS: there is no exception to catch.

stop_rules.STOP-1: cmd_init refuses a blank/whitespace-only --dst BEFORE any normalisation (is_blank(): None, '', or str().strip()==''). A genuinely empty argument is never a valid destination. Exit 2, single-line stderr naming --dst '', no traceback.
stop_rules.STOP-2: After normalisation, guard_destination() refuses a resolved --dst equal to the current working directory, the user home directory, or a filesystem/drive root (is_fs_root(): resolved.parent == resolved). Each refusal is a single stderr line naming the offending path and reason, exit 2.
stop_rules.STOP-3: guard_destination() refuses a resolved --dst equal to the resolved --src; ancestry in BOTH directions is already covered by guard_paths() via _within(): _within(dst, src) is True when dst == src or dst is inside src, and _within(src, dst) is True when dst == src or dst is an ancestor of src. Verified: Path.is_relative_to returns True for equality, so equality AND direct ancestry (src/copy, dst as parent of src) are both refused. The explicit equality check in guard_destination() is defence-in-depth and cannot weaken guard_paths().
stop_rules.STOP-4: Before any removal, cmd_init prints 'round_envelope init: removing existing destination <absolute path>' to stderr, then destroys: the destructive step is visible in logs, not silent.
stop_rules.STOP-5: --allow-destroy (argparse store_true, default OFF) is added and merely permits destroying an existing NON-EMPTY --dst; a non-empty existing dst without the flag is refused (exit 2). STOP-1..STOP-3 are evaluated before this flag and are never bypassed by it (tested with blank and ancestor cases).
stop_rules.STOP-6: Every refusal is a single clean stderr line naming the offending path and the reason, returns exit code 2, and emits no traceback.

other_destructive_subcommands: Only init destroys a directory (shutil.rmtree). snapshot writes files (never removes a directory) and verify only reads/classifies, so no destination guard was added there.
new_helpers: tools/round_envelope.py: is_blank(value), is_fs_root(path), guard_destination(src, dst); cmd_init wires STOP-1..STOP-5; --allow-destroy added to the init subparser; module docstring documents the destruction guards.
tests_added: tests/test_round_envelope.py::DestinationDestructionGuards (7 tests): blank/whitespace dst refuses before normalisation (and never writes scratch); dst == cwd refuses; dst == src refuses; dst ancestor of src refuses; --allow-destroy does not bypass STOP-1..STOP-3 (blank + ancestor); legitimate temp destination still succeeds (positive control); non-empty existing dst needs --allow-destroy and STOP-4 names the removed path. Every destructive-path probe uses a disposable tempfile tree and, where a blank dst is involved, chdirs into a disposable dir so a hypothetical regression could never resolve onto the real tree.
